# Welcome {.unnumbered}

This is a hands-on workshop for modelling **how populations adapt to selection** using the
*EvoDemo-Hyper* matrix population model and its R package, **`evodemohypermpm`**.

The method bridges two traditions that have long talked past each other: **demographers**, who
track populations through matrix models, and **evolutionary quantitative geneticists**, who track
heritable traits through the breeder's equation. The EvoDemo-Hyper MPM does both at once, in a
single, fast, transparent matrix — and lets you ask questions like *"which kind of species adapts
fastest, and does the answer even have a single value?"*

By the end you will be able to:

- run an eco-evolutionary projection for a species of your choice in a single function call;
- read and visualise its output — population size, evolving trait distributions, and adaptation rate;
- compare how the *same* selection pressure plays out across the **slow–fast life-history continuum**;
- understand *why* the answer to "who adapts fastest?" depends on how you define adaptation;
- (going further) see how the hyperstate matrix is built, reproduce the paper's theory-vs-simulation
  comparison, and export your own results to a PDF report.

## Who this is for

Anyone comfortable running R code who is curious about evolutionary demography. **You do not need to
know matrix algebra** to get value from the 2-hour core — we run the model first and open the engine
later. The "Going further" part is for those who want the machinery.

## How this site works

The site is a single reproducible document. Every figure you see was produced by the code printed
just above it, so you can copy any chunk straight into your own session.

::: {.callout-tip title="Three kinds of box appear throughout"}
- **Key idea** boxes flag the one thing to remember from a section.
- **Your turn** boxes are short exercises. Try them before opening the **Solution** — predicting the
  answer first is what makes it stick.
- **Heads-up** boxes warn about a modelling pitfall.
:::

You can read it online, or download the whole thing as a **PDF** from the link in the sidebar.

## Schedule (≈ 2 hours + optional depth)

| | Block | Time | You will… |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | [The big picture](01-big-picture.qmd) | 20 min | meet the life cycle and the model-in-one-picture |
| 2 | [Your first model](02-first-model.qmd) | 30 min | run `MPM()`, read its output, make your first plots |
| 3 | [Selection scenarios](03-selection-scenarios.qmd) | 30 min | put each vital rate under selection and watch traits evolve |
| 4 | [The slow–fast continuum](04-slow-fast.qmd) | 30 min | compare five species and confront the "it depends" punchline |
| ★ | [Under the hood](05-under-the-hood.qmd) | optional | build the hyperstate matrix; theory vs simulation |
| ★ | [Export & extend](06-export-and-extend.qmd) | optional | PDF reports, tuning, and extensions |

Please complete **[Before you arrive](setup.qmd)** so the workshop time is spent modelling, not installing.

## Credit

The method and the R package are the work of **Joanie Van de Walle, Jimmy Garnier, Timothée Bonnet
and Stephanie Jenouvrier** [@vandewalle2025]. This workshop is a teaching layer on top of their
package; please cite the original paper in any work that uses the model.
